title: submit a quantum experiment to an available provider
input: The researcher prepares a supported circuit or optimization task and selects the permitted provider.
action: Azure Quantum coordinates access to supported providers and execution targets through the configured workspace. The chosen provider executes the task; classical experiment code prepares inputs and interprets returned measurements.
output: The research notebook compares accepted results with simulator or classical baselines.
check: Verify target availability, task compatibility, execution status and statistical uncertainty before drawing conclusions.

title: serve an enterprise API from managed OpenShift workers
input: The platform team selects the cluster network, namespaces and approved container image.
action: Azure Red Hat OpenShift provides the supported managed OpenShift platform. OpenShift schedules application pods and serves configured routes; the application validates requests and accesses its restricted data services.
output: The customer invokes the deployed API through the approved route and receives the accepted business result.
check: Test route health, namespace restrictions, pod replacement and data-service access before release.

title: relocate supported application resources to another Region
input: The application owner inventories supported resources and their move dependencies.
action: Resource Mover coordinates the supported preparation and move stages for selected resources. Each resource type has its own prerequisites and move behavior; the owner validates application state and unsupported dependencies separately.
output: The target-region application uses the prepared resources after the approved move or cutover.
check: Check dependency ordering, endpoints, data synchronization and rollback before committing the relocation.

title: investigate an application incident with bounded agent access
input: The incident owner supplies the affected service, symptoms and permitted operational connections.
action: SRE Agent uses supported connected operational context to assist investigation and remediation workflows. Agent permissions and approval settings bound actions; evidence and human validation determine whether a proposed repair is suitable.
output: The responder reviews the diagnosis and executes only the approved repair path.
check: Check causal evidence, resource scope and real application recovery before accepting an agent-assisted action.

title: run a stateful service with partitioned application state
input: The developer supplies the service package, partition model and replication requirements.
action: Service Fabric deploys and manages the configured services, including supported stateful replicas and partitions. Service code executes requests and updates state; partition design determines ownership and scaling boundaries.
output: The application client reaches the intended service partition and receives its accepted operation result.
check: Test replica failure, partition routing, rolling upgrades and recovery of application state.

title: transcribe an authorized support-call recording
input: The application submits permitted audio with the selected language and transcription mode.
action: The selected Speech capability converts supported audio into transcription results under its configured settings. The application aligns the transcript with the call record and validates important names or amounts.
output: The support reviewer uses the transcript to locate relevant call segments and correct material errors.
check: Check language, speaker handling, audio quality, consent and recording retention with representative calls.

title: publish secure appliance telemetry from a managed device
input: The device owner configures supported Sphere hardware, signed application updates and cloud credentials.
action: Azure Sphere combines supported device hardware, operating system and security-service capabilities. The device application reads sensors and connects to its authorized cloud endpoint; platform services support device trust and updates.
output: The receiving application validates telemetry and the approved update channel maintains device software.
check: Test device authentication, signed update acceptance, reconnect behavior and rollback or recovery on the actual board.

title: execute restartable rendering jobs on spare compute
input: The batch owner prepares idempotent render tasks and checkpoints outside the worker VM.
action: Spot VMs provide the selected compute capacity subject to eviction and availability constraints. The worker runs the renderer; the scheduler resubmits interrupted tasks and does not assume the VM will remain available.
output: Completed frames are stored durably before the scheduler marks each task successful.
check: Simulate eviction, duplicate task execution, missing capacity and final frame reconciliation.

title: transition an existing Spring application to a supported hosting target
input: The team inventories Java versions, app bindings, configuration and current Spring Apps dependencies.
action: Spring Apps hosts existing supported Spring workloads during its service lifecycle. Migration recreates runtime configuration and application bindings on the chosen target; the Java code retains its business behavior.
output: The replacement application serves accepted requests using validated database and configuration connections.
check: Compare deployment behavior, secrets, scaling, endpoint response and rollback before moving production traffic.

title: process field data locally before transferring approved output
input: The site owner prepares the supported device workload and its authorized cloud-transfer destination.
action: Stack Edge supplies configured edge compute and data-transfer capabilities on the selected appliance. Local workload code filters or transforms input; the configured transfer path uploads the approved output.
output: The cloud application consumes transferred output while the site retains its local processing and offline procedure.
check: Test local capacity, delayed upload, identity restrictions and recovery when the site loses connectivity.
